_meta.indication: ZELBORAF is indicated for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with BRAF V600E mutation as detected by an FDA-approved test; not recommended for use in patients with wild-type BRAF melanoma

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NO25026 (BRIM3), a randomized, open-label, controlled, multicenter Phase 3 trial of vemurafenib vs dacarbazine
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, open-label trial of ZELBORAF 960 mg orally twice daily versus dacarbazine 1000 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks; randomization stratified by disease stage, LDH, ECOG performance status and geographic region
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive patients with BRAF V600E mutation-positive unresectable or metastatic melanoma as detected by the cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS)
pivotal_trials.result: OS hazard ratio 0.44 (95% CI 0.33, 0.59), p<0.0001; PFS hazard ratio 0.26 (95% CI 0.20, 0.33), p<0.0001 with median PFS 5.3 vs 1.6 months; confirmed response rate 48.4% vs 5.5%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=30%) were arthralgia, rash, alopecia, fatigue, photosensitivity reaction, nausea, pruritus and skin papilloma; in Trial 1 arthralgia 53%, rash 37%, alopecia 45%, fatigue 38%, nausea 35%; cutaneous SCC occurred in 24%. Serious safety signals included cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas, new primary malignant melanomas, liver toxicity, ophthalmologic and cardiac events
target_moa: Vemurafenib is a low molecular weight, orally available kinase inhibitor of some mutated forms of BRAF serine-threonine kinase, including BRAF V600E; some BRAF mutations including V600E result in constitutively activated BRAF proteins
modality: Small molecule (low molecular weight oral kinase inhibitor)
companion_dx_detail: cobas 4800 BRAF V600 Mutation Test, required to detect BRAF V600E mutation for selection of patients appropriate for ZELBORAF therapy

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the benefit/risk profile was clearly favorable for the proposed indication

description.text: Labeling-only update revising Trial 1 median overall survival results and safety information; no change to indication

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes to revise the package insert to: update the Trial 1 median overall survival results in the CLINICAL STUDIES section; update the WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, QT Prolongation section to monitor for QT prolongation prior to and following treatment initiation or after dose modification; relocate the *Cardiac Electrophysiology* subsection to the CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY Pharmacodynamics section; include information regarding hypersensitivity, severe dermatologic reactions, ophthalmologic reactions, hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity in the PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION section; and to update the Medication Guide.

description.text: Updated Clinical Studies with anti-tumor activity data for BRAF V600E mutation-positive melanoma with brain metastases, plus PLLR labeling changes

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes to update the Clinical Studies section to include information from Study MO25743 on the anti-tumor activity of vemurafenib in the treatment of patients with BRAF V600E mutation-positive melanoma with brain metastases; to incorporate revisions to Warnings and Precautions section 5.9, Use in Specific Population sections 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3, Patient Counseling, Section 17, of the package insert, and to the Medication Guide for compliance with Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLRR); and to include editorial changes to Clinical Pharmacology, section 12.1, and Nonclinical Toxicology, sections 13.1 and 13.2, of the package insert.

summary.text: ZELBORAF received Fast Track designation (June 2010) and orphan drug designation, and the NDA was granted priority review because of the improvement in overall survival; it received regular (full) approval based on OS and PFS from the single randomized Phase 3 trial, not accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Fast Track Designation	June 2010	The request for the Fast Track designation was granted on the basis that the product was being investigated to improve overall survival in patients with melanoma containing the BRAFV600E mutation
Vemurafenib is exempt from the requirement for pediatric studies because of orphan drug designation.
Because of the improvement in overall survival, the application was given a priority review designation resulting in a PDUFA date of 10/28/11.

The recommendation for approval is based on the single, randomized clinical trial in which vemurafenib showed statistically significant overall and progression free survival (OS, PFS) advantages over dacarbazine in patients with BRAF V600E mutation-positive unresectable or metastatic melanoma.
